doc.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Style, originality and the younger generation
title: Wynton Marsalis's technique and originality
summary: He thinks Marsalis is the best young technician though a Miles disciple and a polite student of the old-timers.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Have you heard any younger musicians, particularly trumpet players, and some of them are fabulously endowed with technique and very competent on the horn, but have you heard any of this originality that you’re always seeking in anybody that’s come up recently?

Naturally I think Wynton is the best youngster that has come up in a long time so far as technique on his horn. He’s trying everything that the old timers tried and he’s doing that diligently with the plunger and with different mutes. He’s seeking like we did and he does give the old timers a lot of credit for what they’ve done. And he’s a great technician on his horn.
Well, I don’t think he’s what you call an original. Because he’s a Miles Davis disciple. But he’s playing his horn, he’s getting distinctive.
I’ve even heard some things where he sounds a bit like Sweets.

Well, we get together sometimes and he says, “Show me how to do this.” And, I’m quite honored that he would give me that much respect to ask me to show him a few little things on the horn like the valves and the little smears and the delayed things that I love to play. But he’s recognizable.
